correctness.rationale: For nonscalar \(x\in M_2(\mathbf F_q)\), the minimal polynomial has degree two, hence \(C_R(x)=\operatorname{span}\{I,x\}\) and \(|C_R(x)|=q^2\). Cyclicity of trace gives \(\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{ad}_x)\subseteq C_R(x)^\perp\), and both spaces have dimension two, so equality holds. For traceless \(r\), this makes \(r\in[x,R]\) equivalent to \(\operatorname{tr}(rx)=0\). For nonzero \(r\) the latter is a nonzero linear functional with a \(q^3\)-element kernel; exactly the \(q\) scalar matrices in that kernel cannot have a nonzero commutator fiber, leaving \(q^3-q\) exceptional vertices. Each nonempty fiber is an affine coset of the \(q^2\)-element centralizer. Substituting these facts into Nath–Sharma–Dutta–Shang's published degree formula yields the stated characteristic-two and odd-characteristic degree values. The \(r=0\) and nontraceless cases follow from the same centralizer count and the trace-zero property of every additive commutator.

originality.rationale: The exact degree multiset is a direct specialization of a published general theorem plus standard two-by-two matrix algebra. Nath–Sharma–Dutta–Shang already prove that the degree is determined by whether \(T_{x,r}\) is empty and, when nonempty, by \(|C_R(x)|\). For a nonscalar two-by-two matrix, the centralizer is the two-dimensional polynomial algebra in \(x\); the trace-pairing adjoint identity then gives \(\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{ad}_x)=C_R(x)^\perp\) by a one-line dimension count. Thus the hyperplane criterion, the \(q^3-q\) count, and the displayed degree multiplicities follow mechanically. Under the audit's implication rule, lack of the exact matrix-ring wording in the graph paper does not make this corollary original.
